description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's Burundi Country Programme works to strengthen Burundi's trade competitiveness and deepen its integration into regional and global markets, building on over a decade of engagement since 2011. The Programme supports modernisation of trade systems and institutions, including continued collaboration with the Burundi Revenue Authority (OBR) on customs digitisation and the Electronic Single Window, while advancing the competitiveness of key export value chains such as coffee, tea, and horticulture. Interventions also target the trade and investment environment through AfCFTA alignment, standards accreditation via the Bureau Burundais de Normalisation et Contrôle de la Qualité (BBN), and expanded market access for SMEs, with a deliberate focus on inclusive participation including women traders and cross-border trade actors.

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.

title.narrative: Efficient trade through innovative digital technologies
Revenue collected attributable to ASYCUDA supported by TMA​

comment.narrative: 45% increase in customs revenue on ASYCUDA due to digitisation. Customs revenue grew from BIF 584 billion ($ 292 million) in 2021–2022 to BIF 849 billion ($ 425 million) in 2023–2024.

title.narrative: Average time taken processing of trade documents while moving goods (approval times for pharmaceutical import permits)

description.narrative: Time in days taken to process trade document

comment.narrative: 100 eSW end users trained on the new web-based modules- leading to atleast 5% reduction in processing time

80% reduction in approval times for pharmaceutical import permits, from 5 days in 2019 to under 24 hours in 2023 after upgrading the Burundi Electronic Single Window. The system has streamlined processes in key agencies including the Investment Promotion Agency (import permits and export certificates), Ministry of Health and Ministry of Agriculture (farm-related imports and exports).
